title: Function Parameters, Return Values, and Scope

content.title: Positional vs Keyword Arguments
content.explanation: Arguments can be passed by position or by keyword name. Keyword arguments make code more readable and allow skipping optional parameters.
key_points: Keyword: func(a=1, b=2) - matches by name
Can mix: func(1, b=2) - positional first!

content.title: Argument Passing Examples
content.explanation: Keyword arguments can be in any order. Default parameter city makes it optional.

content.title: Multiple Return Values
content.explanation: Python functions can return multiple values by returning a tuple. The caller can unpack into multiple variables. This is idiomatic Python.
key_points: return a, b, c  # Returns tuple (a, b, c)
x, y, z = func()  # Tuple unpacking
Use for related values (min, max), (quotient, remainder)

content.title: Multiple Return Examples
content.explanation: Returning comma-separated values creates a tuple. Unpacking assigns each to a variable.

content.title: Variable Scope: LEGB Rule
content.explanation: Python uses LEGB rule for variable lookup: Local -> Enclosing -> Global -> Built-in. Assignment creates local variable unless declared global/nonlocal.

content.title: Scope Examples
content.code:
print(x)  # local
    inner()
    print(x)  # enclosing

outer()
print(x)  # global

# Modifying global
def modify_global():
    global x
    x =
content.explanation: Each function creates its own local scope. global declares module-level intent. nonlocal for enclosing scope.

content.title: Scope Prediction
content.question: What are the two outputs?
content.explanation: func() creates local x=20, prints 20. Global x unchanged at 10.

content.title: Fix the Scope Bug
content.buggy_code:
count = 0
def increment():
    count += 1

increment()
print(count)
content.error_message: UnboundLocalError: local variable 'count' referenced before assignment
content.task: Fix the function to modify the global count
content.hint: Use global keyword to declare you mean the global variable
content.solution:
count = 0
def increment():
    global count
    count += 1

increment()
print(count)  # 1

exercises.title: Multiple Returns
exercises.description: Write a function stats(numbers) that returns (count, total, average) for a list of numbers.
exercises.starter_code:
def stats(numbers):
    # Return count, sum, average
exercises.solution:
def stats(numbers):
    count = len(numbers)
    total = sum(numbers)
    average = total / count if count > 0 else 0
    return count, total, average

c, t, a = stats([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
print(c, t, a)  # 5 15 3.0
hints: Use len(), sum(), return three values

exercises.title: Scope Practice
exercises.description:
Predict the output of this code, then run to verify:
x = 1
def f():
    x = 2
    def g():
        nonlocal x
        x = 3
    g()
    print(x)
f()
print(x)
exercises.solution:
x = 1
def f():
    x = 2
    def g():
        nonlocal x
        x = 3
    g()
    print(x)  # 3
f()
print(x)  # 1
hints: nonlocal modifies enclosing scope, not global
